Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Time, the calendar & feasts

cycle noun

a series that comes round again

also cycles, cyclical, the cycle of the seasons, life cycle, round

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.45
Cic. N.D. 2.52: a planet eundem duodecim signōrum orbem annīs duodecim cōnficit (Lewis & Short)

orbis, orbis m.

noun, third declension

a round, a cycle

Properly a circle or ring, and so the round that a star or a course of events goes through and comes back from: orbem cōnficere, to complete a cycle. Its other everyday senses are a disc or round surface, and the world (orbis terrārum).

Other words

  • circuitus, circuitūs m. — a going round, a revolution; a periodic return

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.49: sōlis (Lewis & Short); Cels. 3.5: the periodic return of a fever (Lewis & Short)

    More often a way round, a circuit or detour (Caes., Liv.).

  • vicissitūdō, vicissitūdinis f. — alternation, the coming round of each in turn

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.16

    For things that take turns, as day and night or the seasons, rather than a single round.

  • cyclus, cyclī m. — a cycle (in astronomy and the calendar)

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Isid. Orig. 6.17.1: cyclus paschālis (Lewis & Short)

    A Greek word, late and technical: the Easter cycle, the lunar cycle. Lewis & Short marks its y as common, so it is left unmarked.

Examples

  • mīrīque sunt orbēs et quasi circuitūs in rēbus pūblicīs commūtātiōnum et vicissitūdinum

    and there are remarkable cycles and, as it were, rounds of change and alternation in statesCic. Rep. 1.45

  • quem vērō astrōrum ōrdinēs, quem diērum noctiumque vicissitūdinēs … nōn grātum esse cōgunt

    but someone whom the order of the stars, the alternation of days and nights … do not make gratefulCic. Leg. 2.16

See also development cycle, season, year, day.
